75: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
76: 
77: ### Problem Statement
78: A speckit command tells a writer where to find authoring guidance, how a placeholder is treated and which files a packet holds. Six of those statements are now wrong or incomplete, and the same wrong text is copied into seven runtime trees. A weak model reads the command, follows the stale line and produces the defect that phases 2 to 5 just fixed in the templates.

80: ### Purpose
81: One corrected command and agent surface, with every runtime mirror regenerated from it, so a writer sees the same rule no matter which command or runtime it uses.

93: - Eight read-only mirror checks and three read-only doctor:speckit checks.

96: ### Out of Scope
97: - Template, validator, runtime source and reference edits. Phases 2 to 5 and 7 own those.
98: - Implementing `check-example-drift.sh` or `check-card-sync.sh`. Phase 5 owns both. This phase only names them in commands.
99: - Release, update and compat engine behavior. `/doctor:update` is audited for stale statements and changed only if the audit finds one.
100: - Hand edits to a generated mirror. The generators own those files.

103: 
104: | File Path | Change Type | Description |

113: | `.claude/agents/markdown.md`, `orchestrate.md`, `code.md`, `context.md` | Modify | Same body text, so the agent mirror check stays green |
114: | `.codex/agents/*.toml`, `.codex/prompts/*.md`, `.pi/agents/*.md`, `.pi/prompts/*.md` | Regenerate | Generated mirrors of the corrected sources |
115: | `scratch/audit/*`, `scratch/mirrors/*`, `scratch/suite-*.txt`, `scratch/review/*` | Create | Evidence for every gate |

149: 
150: - **SC-001**: A writer who opens any speckit command sees the authoring card named before the long references and the filled example named before the template source.
151: - **SC-002**: A grep for the retired checklist doc over the command and agent surface prints nothing, so no reader is sent to a file that no longer exists.
152: - **SC-003**: Every runtime mirror check exits 0 on the corrected tree, so no runtime carries a different rule from another.

158: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
159: 
160: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
161: |------|------|--------|------------|
162: | Dependency | Authoring card and two guard scripts from phases 2 and 5 | The A1 rows and the A5 rows cannot be applied | Every dependent row carries a pre-check command, and a failed pre-check records the row as `SKIP-MISSING` |
163: | Dependency | Phase 1 ledger | A census row that this phase owns could be missed | `tasks.md` T010 reads every ledger row with `owner_phase` 006 and records it against the audit table |
164: | Risk | An agent body edit leaves the Claude sibling behind | `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs` fails and the phase blocks | The 6 mirror rows apply the same text to `.claude/agents`, and the check runs before the suite |
165: | Risk | A mirror generator rewrites an unrelated file | The scope check reports a path no row explains | The scope check in `tasks.md` T011 compares the changed set with the row file set and the generated set |
166: | Risk | The trigger index is already stale at the phase start | A literal freshness gate would fail for a reason this phase did not cause | T009 compares the staleness set before and after, not the freshness bit |
167: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: 
172: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
173: 
174: ### Performance
175: - **NFR-P01**: The 27 rows are applied by script in one pass, with no model call. The only model call in the phase is the single read-only frontier review.
176: 
177: ### Security
178: - **NFR-S01**: No brief, row or scratch file carries a credential, token or key. The review runs with a read-only sandbox.
179: 
180: ### Reliability
181: - **NFR-R01**: A second apply of any row fails, because the locator is gone. A rerun therefore cannot edit a file twice.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 8. EDGE CASES
186: 
187: ### Data Boundaries
188: - Empty input: a row whose `locator` count is 0 is recorded as `SKIP-GONE` and the phase continues, because an earlier phase may have fixed the same line.
189: - Maximum length: a row whose `expected_text` holds more than one line is applied as one replacement, and the JSONL encoder writes the line breaks as `\n`.
190: 
191: ### Error Scenarios
192: - External service failure: the frontier review is the only external call. A provider error is recorded with its stderr, and REQ-008 stays open.
193: - Network timeout: the review is retried once, then recorded as skipped.
194: - Pre-check failure: a row whose pre-check command exits non-zero is recorded as `SKIP-MISSING` and is not applied.
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
199: 
200: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
201: |-----------|-------|----------|
202: | Scope | 10/25 | Files: 12 authored, 4 Claude siblings, 4 generated trees. Systems: commands, agents, mirrors |
203: | Risk | 5/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N |
204: | Research | 8/20 | The audit was done at authoring time against the real tree |
205: | Multi-Agent | 4/15 | Workstreams: 1 conductor, 1 review |
206: | Coordination | 8/15 | Dependencies: phases 1, 2 and 5 |
207: | **Total** | **35/100** | **Level 3** |
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
212: 
213: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
214: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
215: | R-001 | A row is applied to the wrong line because the text drifted | H | L | The applier refuses unless the locator occurs exactly once, and T004 checks all 27 counts before T006 |
216: | R-002 | A mirror is hand-edited and the next generator run reverts it | M | L | T008 runs the generators, and the checks prove the generated tree matches the source |
217: | R-003 | The pre-existing stale trigger index is mistaken for a defect of this phase | M | M | T009 compares the staleness set before and after |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 11. USER STORIES
222: 
223: ### US-001: The short card comes first (Priority: P0)
224: 
225: **As a** weak model writing a spec doc, **I want** the command I am following to name the short authoring card and a filled example, **so that** I do not open a 1,200-line guide or a template with unfilled sections.
226: 
227: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
228: 
229: ---
230: 
231: ### US-002: Every runtime agrees (Priority: P0)
232: 
233: **As the** operator, **I want** every runtime tree regenerated from one corrected source, **so that** a writer on Claude, Codex, Pi or OpenCode reads the same rule.
234: 
235: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
240: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
241: 
242: - None that block this phase. Every choice it needs is frozen in `goal.md` section 1.
243: - The trigger index is stale at the phase start for reasons outside this phase. T009 records the exact set and does not try to fix it.
244: - The suite already differs from phase 1's `suite-start.txt` because phases 2 to 5 added tests. T012 compares against the phase start and records the cumulative delta as information.
245: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: ## RELATED DOCUMENTS
250: 
251: - **Implementation Plan**: See `plan.md`
252: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
253: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
254: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
255:

335: ### The applier
336: 
337: `scratch/tools/apply_row.py` is the phase 2 script with one added refusal, written in `tasks.md` T005. It reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so an append-style row cannot apply twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once. It replaces that one occurrence and prints `APPLIED <id> <file>`. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1.
338: 
339: `scratch/tools/lib.sh` adds `apply_checked`, which prints the applier result and a `CHECK <id> extra_paths=<n>` line. `extra_paths` counts changed paths the row does not name. It must be 0 for every row.

341: ### Mirror mechanics
342: 
343: | Tree | Role | How it is produced | How it is checked |
344: |------|------|--------------------|-------------------|
345: | `.skilled/commands` | Canonical command source | Authored here | Not generated |
346: | `.opencode/commands` | OpenCode view | Symlink to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
347: | `.claude/commands` | Claude view | Per-file symlinks to `.skilled/commands` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` |
348: | `.skilled/agents` | Canonical OpenCode agent source | Authored here, also reached as `.opencode/agents` | Not generated |
349: | `.claude/agents` | Authored Claude sibling | Edited by the six MIRROR rows, no generator | `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` |
350: | `.cursor/agents`, `.devin/agents` | Cursor and Devin views | Symlinks to `.claude/agents` | `sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check` and the roster check |
351: | `.codex/agents` | Codex TOML | `sync-agents.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents.cjs --check` |
352: | `.codex/prompts` | Codex command stubs | `sync-prompts.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts.cjs --check` |
353: | `.pi/agents` | Pi agent copies | `sync-agents-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/agents` | `sync-agents-pi.cjs --check` |
354: | `.pi/prompts` | Pi command stubs | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs` from `.skilled/commands` | `sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check` |

356: Never hand-edit `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`. Run the generator named in the table. The `.claude/agents` tree is the one authored sibling, and the six MIRROR rows are its scripted edit.

358: ### Data Flow
359: `rows.jsonl` goes through `apply_row.py`, one row at a time. Each apply is followed by a changed-path check. The four searches then prove the stale text is gone. The generators rebuild the generated trees, the eight checks prove they agree, and the diff goes through the scope check, the suite comparison and the frontier review.

428: 
429: - **Trigger**: a changed path that no row and no generator explains. Or a mirror check that stays red after one generator rerun. Or a suite difference that survives one rerun.

643: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
644: 
645: ### ADR-001: Freeze the audit as exact rows and apply it by script
646: 
647: **Status**: Accepted
648: 
649: **Context**: The audit found 21 stale statements in 12 files. A weak model asked to fix them from a description may reword the new text, change a neighbouring line or skip one. The same text must land in four Claude agent bodies without a second judgment.
650: 
651: **Decision**: Every change is frozen at authoring time as a row with a locator and an exact replacement. `apply_row.py` makes every change and refuses unless the locator occurs exactly once. No model edits a file in this phase.
652: 
653: **Consequences**:
654: - The 27 rows cost no model call, and each one is checked by its own counts.
655: - A second apply fails, so a retry can never edit twice.
656: - A row whose text drifted is skipped and recorded, not guessed.
657: 
658: **Alternatives Rejected**:
659: - A worker reads each file and edits the prose: it can paraphrase, and the audit would then differ from the text this packet reviewed.
660: - `sed -i` one-liners: the quoting of backticks, pipes and quotes in these lines is the exact place a weak model slips, and `sed` replaces every match without a count check.
661: 
662: ### ADR-002: Edit the authored Claude sibling by row, then regenerate the generated trees
663: 
664: **Status**: Accepted
665: 
666: **Context**: `.claude/agents` is an authored tree in the Claude dialect, not a generated one. `.codex` and `.pi` are generated from `.skilled/agents`. Editing `.skilled/agents` alone leaves the Claude body behind, and `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs` reports drift.
667: 
668: **Decision**: Six MIRROR rows apply the same body text to `.claude/agents`. The `.codex` and `.pi` trees are rebuilt by their generators. No one hand-edits `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`.
669: 
670: **Consequences**:
671: - The agent mirror check passes on the corrected tree.
672: - The Claude sibling stays an authored file, so a future agent change must repeat this two-step shape.
673: 
674: **Alternatives Rejected**:
675: - Hand-edit `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.pi/agents/*.md`: the next generator run reverts them, and the hand edit hides the drift until then.
676: - Skip the Claude sibling: `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` fails and the phase cannot close.
677: 
678: ### ADR-003: Compare the suite and the trigger index with the phase start, not with phase 1
679: 
680: **Status**: Accepted
681: 
682: **Context**: Phase 1 recorded `suite-start.txt` before any template changed. Phases 2 to 5 add tests, so a literal match with phase 1 would block on tests this phase did not write. The trigger index is already stale at the phase start for reasons outside this phase, so a freshness gate would block on a pre-existing condition.
683: 
684: **Decision**: The suite gate compares the `Test Files`, `Tests` and `exit=` lines at the phase start with the same lines at close. The trigger-index gate compares the staleness set before and after. Both record the cumulative difference against phase 1 as information, not as a pass condition.
685: 
686: **Consequences**:
687: - A regression this phase introduces is caught.
688: - A known difference from an earlier phase is reported, not mistaken for a defect.
689: - The conductor cannot claim a clean phase-1 match, and the plan says so.
690: 
691: **Alternatives Rejected**:
692: - Require an exact phase-1 match: it fails on the tests phases 2 to 5 added, and a weak executor would then try to delete them.
693: - Require `fresh: true` from the trigger index: the index is stale before the phase starts, so the gate would be red on arrival.

335: ### The applier
336: 
337: `scratch/tools/apply_row.py` is the phase 2 script with one added refusal, written in `tasks.md` T005. It reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so an append-style row cannot apply twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once. It replaces that one occurrence and prints `APPLIED <id> <file>`. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1.
338: 
339: `scratch/tools/lib.sh` adds `apply_checked`, which prints the applier result and a `CHECK <id> extra_paths=<n>` line. `extra_paths` counts changed paths the row does not name. It must be 0 for every row.

343: | Tree | Role | How it is produced | How it is checked |

345: | `.skilled/commands` | Canonical command source | Authored here | Not generated |

The generators rebuild the generated trees, the eight checks prove they agree, and the diff goes through the scope check, the suite comparison and the frontier review.

427: ## 7. ROLLBACK PLAN

643: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
644: 
645: ### ADR-001: Freeze the audit as exact rows and apply it by script
646: 
647: **Status**: Accepted
648: 
649: **Context**: The audit found 21 stale statements in 12 files. A weak model asked to fix them from a description may reword the new text, change a neighbouring line or skip one. The same text must land in four Claude agent bodies without a second judgment.
650: 
651: **Decision**: Every change is frozen at authoring time as a row with a locator and an exact replacement. `apply_row.py` makes every change and refuses unless the locator occurs exactly once. No model edits a file in this phase.
652: 
653: **Consequences**:
654: - The 27 rows cost no model call, and each one is checked by its own counts.
655: - A second apply fails, so a retry can never edit twice.
656: - A row whose text drifted is skipped and recorded, not guessed.
657: 
658: **Alternatives Rejected**:
659: - A worker reads each file and edits the prose: it can paraphrase, and the audit would then differ from the text this packet reviewed.
660: - `sed -i` one-liners: the quoting of backticks, pipes and quotes in these lines is the exact place a weak model slips, and `sed` replaces every match without a count check.
661: 
662: ### ADR-002: Edit the authored Claude sibling by row, then regenerate the generated trees
663: 
664: **Status**: Accepted
665: 
666: **Context**: `.claude/agents` is an authored tree in the Claude dialect, not a generated one. `.codex` and `.pi` are generated from `.skilled/agents`. Editing `.skilled/agents` alone leaves the Claude body behind, and `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs` reports drift.
667: 
668: **Decision**: Six MIRROR rows apply the same body text to `.claude/agents`. The `.codex` and `.pi` trees are rebuilt by their generators. No one hand-edits `.codex`, `.pi`, `.cursor` or `.devin`.
669: 
670: **Consequences**:
671: - The agent mirror check passes on the corrected tree.
672: - The Claude sibling stays an authored file, so a future agent change must repeat this two-step shape.
673: 
674: **Alternatives Rejected**:
675: - Hand-edit `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.pi/agents/*.md`: the next generator run reverts them, and the hand edit hides the drift until then.
676: - Skip the Claude sibling: `check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all` fails and the phase cannot close.
677: 
678: ### ADR-003: Compare the suite and the trigger index with the phase start, not with phase 1
679: 
680: **Status**: Accepted
681: 
682: **Context**: Phase 1 recorded `suite-start.txt` before any template changed. Phases 2 to 5 add tests, so a literal match with phase 1 would block on tests this phase did not write. The trigger index is already stale at the phase start for reasons outside this phase, so a freshness gate would block on a pre-existing condition.
683: 
684: **Decision**: The suite gate compares the `Test Files`, `Tests` and `exit=` lines at the phase start with the same lines at close. The trigger-index gate compares the staleness set before and after. Both record the cumulative difference against phase 1 as information, not as a pass condition.
685: 
686: **Consequences**:
687: - A regression this phase introduces is caught.
688: - A known difference from an earlier phase is reported, not mistaken for a defect.
689: - The conductor cannot claim a clean phase-1 match, and the plan says so.
690: 
691: **Alternatives Rejected**:
692: - Require an exact phase-1 match: it fails on the tests phases 2 to 5 added, and a weak executor would then try to delete them.
693: - Require `fresh: true` from the trigger index: the index is stale before the phase starts, so the gate would be red on arrival.
694:

111: - [ ] T005 Save the tools, then test the applier on a copy (`scratch/tools/apply_row.py`, `scratch/tools/check_rows.py`, `scratch/tools/lib.sh`). Run the four heredocs below, then the self-test. Verify: the self-test prints, in order, a line that starts with `APPLIED R-001`, a line that starts with `FAIL R-001: expected text already present`, `exit=1`, and `1`. The last number is the count of changed lines in the copy, so it proves the applier changed one line and ran only once. Then `bash -n "$PHASE/scratch/tools/lib.sh" && echo SYNTAX_OK` prints `SYNTAX_OK`.
112: 
113:   `apply_row.py` reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root directory. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so a second apply cannot append or replace twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once in the row's file. It replaces that one occurrence, prints `APPLIED <id> <file>` and exits 0. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1. The expected-text guard is the reason a second apply fails, because an append-style row keeps its old text as a prefix and the locator alone would still occur once.
114: 
115: ```bash
116: cd "$WORKTREE"
117: cat > "$PHASE/scratch/tools/apply_row.py" <<'PY'
118: import json, sys
119: ledger, row_id = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
120: root = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "."
121: rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ledger, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
122: match = [r for r in rows if r["id"] == row_id]
123: if len(match) != 1:
124:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: expected 1 ledger row, found {len(match)}")
125: r = match[0]
126: if r["expected_text"] in ("OWNED BY PHASE", "DELETE FILE"):
127:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: not a text replacement ({r['expected_text']})")
128: path = f"{root}/{r['file']}"
129: text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
130: if r["expected_text"] in text:
131:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: expected text already present in {r['file']}")
132: count = text.count(r["locator"])
133: if count != 1:
134:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: locator found {count} times in {r['file']}")
135: open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(r["locator"], r["expected_text"], 1))
136: print(f"APPLIED {row_id} {r['file']}")
137: PY
138: ```

113:   `apply_row.py` reads a ledger path, a row id and an optional root directory. It refuses a row whose `expected_text` is `OWNED BY PHASE` or `DELETE FILE`. It refuses when the expected text is already in the file, so a second apply cannot append or replace twice. It refuses unless the `locator` occurs exactly once in the row's file. It replaces that one occurrence, prints `APPLIED <id> <file>` and exits 0. Every refusal prints `FAIL <id>: <reason>` and exits 1. The expected-text guard is the reason a second apply fails, because an append-style row keeps its old text as a prefix and the locator alone would still occur once.

121: rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(ledger, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]

132: count = text.count(r["locator"])
133: if count != 1:
134:     sys.exit(f"FAIL {row_id}: locator found {count} times in {r['file']}")
135: open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text.replace(r["locator"], r["expected_text"], 1))

66: | [Uncertainty and honesty](.skilled/repo-rules/uncertainty-and-honesty.md) | Never fabricate; mark the confidence you actually have and halt on a contradiction. |

69: | [Communication prose](.skilled/repo-rules/communication-prose.md) | How a sentence reads: sentence and paragraph shape, plain words, punctuation. |

79: ## 4. SCOPE OF THIS DOCUMENT
80: 
81: **In:** how to think and act, restraint, scope, evidence, risk, diagnosis, honesty,
82: the posture to hold when work is handed to another runtime, how the resulting reply
83: reads, what you may claim about wiring you have changed, and how a turn hands control
84: back to the operator. The delegation posture was the first widening and Delivery the
85: second, added when `AGENTS.md` §8 moved down. Delivery is one of two rules here whose
86: trigger is a whole turn rather than a specific action, the other being the handback rule,
87: which fires at every turn's end, and §8 keeps the two clauses that must bind even when
88: nothing loads.
89: 
90: **Out:** skill routing, workflow selection, spec-folder mechanics, and the *mechanics*
91: of agent and CLI dispatch: which agent, which command, which model, which flags.
92: Those belong to `AGENTS.md` §2 and the skills it routes to, and are deliberately
93: absent here so each has exactly one place to change. The line is between plumbing and
94: posture: how to dispatch is theirs, how to think while dispatching is ours.
95:

97: route stays Out. *Verifying wiring you changed, and what you may claim about it*, is
98: In; it is an evidence obligation whose subject happens to be routing. `skill-hub-routing.md`
99: is the one rule on this side of that line, and it carries no route-selection guidance:
100: the mechanics stay in the skills, and the rule points at them. A fourth widening that
101: admits selection itself would dissolve the boundary; this one does not.
102: 
103: **The ask-surface carve-out, added as the fourth widening, on an operator decision that
104: overrode a research refusal.** A four-iteration decision-test run returned *refuse* here:
105: naming a question tool per runtime reads as the "which command" family, and the paragraph
106: above pre-refuses a fourth widening that admits selection. The operator widened it anyway,
107: and what follows is the narrowing that keeps the boundary standing. *Choosing between
108: runtimes, agents, commands, models or flags* stays Out, unchanged. *Naming the surface that
109: asks the operator a question, in the runtime you are already running in*, is In. That is not
110: a selection, because nothing is being selected: the runtime is a given, and the rule records
111: which of its surfaces carries an obligation the rule already imposes. `communication-handoff.md`
112: is the one rule on this side of that line, its §5 is the only place a tool name appears, and
113: it names only what this repository confirms. A fifth widening that let a rule pick between
114: runtimes would be the dissolution this one avoids.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: CHECK PLACEHOLDERS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Scan spec folder .md files for remaining bracket placeholder
# Patterns after upgrade-level.sh + auto-populate.
# Bash 3.2+ compatible (macOS and Linux).
#
# This is the broad post-edit scan the quality hook runs: any bracket that
# still looks like a template placeholder. The validator rule at
# rules/check-placeholders.sh is narrower on purpose, flagging only the two
# canonical markers, so the two are not the same check with two homes.

set -euo pipefail

VERSION="1.0.0"

# Colors (disabled for non-TTY)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m' GREEN='\033[0;32m' YELLOW='\033[1;33m' BOLD='\033[1m' NC='\033[0m'
else
    RED='' GREEN='' YELLOW='' BOLD='' NC=''
fi

# ─── Usage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") <spec-folder> [OPTIONS]

Scan a spec folder for remaining bracket placeholder patterns.

Arguments:
  <spec-folder>    Path to spec folder (e.g., specs/042-feature/)

Options:
  --json           Output results in JSON format
  --verbose        Show each match with file and line number
  --help, -h       Show this help message

Exit codes:
  0  No placeholders found (PASS)
  1  Placeholders found (FAIL)
  2  Invalid arguments or folder not found

Examples:
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --verbose
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --json
EOF
}

# ─── Args ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FOLDER_PATH=""
JSON_MODE=false
VERBOSE=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --json)     JSON_MODE=true; shift ;;
        --verbose)  VERBOSE=true; shift ;;
        --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
        -*)         echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
                FOLDER_PATH="$1"
            else
                echo "Error: unexpected argument '$1'" >&2
                usage >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: spec folder path required" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 2
fi

# Normalize trailing slash
FOLDER_PATH="${FOLDER_PATH%/}"

if [[ ! -d "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: folder not found: $FOLDER_PATH" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# ─── Placeholder patterns ────────────────────────────────────
# Match bracket patterns that look like template placeholders:
#   [Response time target], [Low/Med/High], [Component A],
#   [YOUR_VALUE_HERE], [PLACEHOLDER], etc.
#
# The templates write their stubs with the example inline, as in
# [Response time target - e.g., <200ms p95], [Uptime target - e.g., 99.9%]
# and [What problem we're solving], so the body admits < > + % and the
# apostrophe too. Without them those stubs pass the scan unfilled.
PLACEHOLDER_BODY="[A-Za-z0-9 /,._<>+%'-]"
#
# Exclude patterns that are NOT placeholders:
#   [x] / [ ] (checkbox), [P0] / [P1] / [P2] (priority tags),
#   [SPECKIT...] (markers), [ANCHOR...] (anchors),
#   [EVIDENCE...] (checklist evidence), [W:...] (workstream),
#   [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] (spec markers), [B] (blocked task)
#
# Also exclude lines where brackets appear inside code blocks
# (backtick-wrapped) since those describe placeholder concepts
# Rather than being actual unfilled placeholders.

TOTAL=0
MATCHES=""

# Process each .md file (skip backup/temp directories)
while IFS= read -r file; do
    # Skip backup directories and non-template subfolders.
    # Memory/ contains generated session context markdown that legitimately
    # Uses bracketed TOC links (e.g., [CONTINUE SESSION]); scratch/ is temp.
    case "$file" in
        */.backup-*) continue ;;
        */memory/*) continue ;;
        */scratch/*) continue ;;
        # research/ and review/ hold the deep loops' own output: iteration files,
        # dashboards and syntheses their workflow writes and regenerates, where
        # bracketed status text such as [None yet] is the reducer's format rather
        # than an unfilled template. The validator's placeholder rule reads only
        # the authored docs, so this scan matches it.
        */research/*) continue ;;
        */review/*) continue ;;
    esac

    line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))

        # Skip lines inside code fences or with backtick-wrapped brackets
        case "$line" in
            '```'*) continue ;;
            *'`['*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Skip HTML comments
        case "$line" in
            *'<!--'*'-->'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Match bracket patterns that look like placeholders
        # Use grep to find [Something here] patterns
        if echo "$line" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}+\]" 2>/dev/null; then
            # Exclude known non-placeholder patterns
            cleaned="$line"
            # Remove known safe patterns before re-checking
            cleaned=$(echo "$cleaned" | sed -E \
                -e 's/\[x\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ \]//g' \
                -e 's/\[P[0-2]\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[B\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[SPECKIT[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ANCHOR[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[EVIDENCE[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[W:[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/`[^`]*`//g' \
                -e 's/\[[^]]*\]\(//g' \
            )

            # Check if any placeholder-like patterns remain after cleanup
            if echo "$cleaned" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null; then
                TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
                match_text=$(echo "$line" | grep -oE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
                if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]]; then
                    MATCHES="${MATCHES}  ${file}:${line_num}: ${match_text}\n"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done < "$file"
done < <(find "$FOLDER_PATH" -name "*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort)

# ─── Output ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$JSON_MODE" == "true" ]]; then
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "{\"status\":\"PASS\",\"placeholders\":0,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    else
        echo "{\"status\":\"FAIL\",\"placeholders\":$TOTAL,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    fi
else
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}PASS${NC} — Zero placeholder patterns found in ${FOLDER_PATH}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}${BOLD}FAIL${NC} — ${TOTAL} placeholder pattern(s) found in ${FOLDER_PATH}" >&2
        if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" && -n "$MATCHES" ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo -e "$MATCHES"
        fi
    fi
fi

# Exit code: 0 = pass, 1 = fail
if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
    exit 0

Usage: $(basename "$0") <spec-folder> [OPTIONS]

<skill_content name="sk-doc">
# Skill: sk-doc

<!-- Keywords: sk-doc, documentation, markdown, authoring, parent-hub, mode-registry, hub-router, workflowmode, packetkind, sk-create-skill, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command, sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark, sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter, sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, sk-create-quality-control, human-voice-rules, hvr, shared-backbone, create-quality-control-pipeline -->

# Documentation Authoring Hub (sk-doc)

One advisor identity, fifteen workflow modes across fourteen packets, one shared sk-create-quality-control backbone. `sk-doc` is the parent hub for documentation and OpenCode-component authoring. It holds NO per-packet logic: it routes by `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json`, and each packet keeps its own contract in its nested folder. The cross-cutting sk-create-quality-control pipeline (validators, global standards, frontmatter/llms/template assets) lives once in `shared/` and is consumed by every packet.

**Version authority.** This file's `version` frontmatter is the hub's release version and matches the newest entry under `changelog/`; `description.json`, `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` carry the same value, so every hub-root JSON routing file states the same release; `ROUTER.md` keeps its own document version.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Use this skill for documentation and OpenCode-component authoring, and for document-quality work. The hub classifies the request, resolves a `workflowMode`, and loads the matching nested packet.

| Mode | Use it for | Packet | Command |
|------|------------|--------|---------|
| **sk-create-skill** | Scaffold an OpenCode skill (and, via `sk-create-skill-parent`, a parent hub with nested mode packets) | `sk-create-skill/` | `/create:skill`, `/create:skill-parent` |
| **sk-create-readme** | Author a folder README, general or code-folder | `sk-create-readme/` | `/create:readme` |
| **sk-create-agent** | Scaffold an OpenCode agent (permission/authority frontmatter) | `sk-create-agent/` | `/create:agent` |
| **sk-create-command** | Scaffold an OpenCode slash command (argument-hint + allowed-tools + router/presentation split) | `sk-create-command/` | `/create:command` |
| **sk-create-feature-catalog** | Author a feature-catalog inventory package | `sk-create-feature-catalog/` | `/create:feature-catalog` |
| **sk-create-manual-testing-playbook** | Author a manual-testing-playbook package | `sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/` | `/create:manual-testing-playbook` |
| **sk-create-benchmark** | Author MCP-promotion and behavior packages or inputs | `sk-create-benchmark/` | `/create:benchmark` |
| **sk-create-changelog** | Author a global or packet-local changelog entry (version bump + topology-aware placement) | `sk-create-changelog/` | `/create:changelog` |
| **sk-create-diff** | Produce a local, Git-free before/after review of an edited document (text/Markdown/HTML/DOCX/text-PDF) as a self-contained HTML report | `sk-create-diff/` | `/create:diff` |
| **sk-create-repo-rule** | Create, revise or retire a repo-local rule under `repo-rules/` and wire it into `REPO RULES.md` (four decision tests refuse most requests) | `sk-create-repo-rule/` | `/create:repo-rule` |
| **sk-create-with-human-voice** | Apply the Human Voice Rules to prose, or score prose against them, with a scope gate and a re-scan | `sk-create-with-human-voice/` | `/create:with-human-voice` |
| **sk-create-frontmatter** | Own the YAML frontmatter contract: per-class field rules, the description budget, and the 4-part `version` derivation | `sk-create-frontmatter/` | — (routes via aliases) |
| **sk-create-goal** | Author or revise a packet `goal.md`: the durable directive, three to seven self-contained completion criteria, and the phase-parent binding table (session-goal setting stays with the goal hooks) | `sk-create-goal/` | `/create:goal` |
| **sk-create-quality-control** | Validate / score / optimize an EXISTING document (extract → DQI → HVR → validate) | `sk-create-quality-control/` | (routes via aliases) |

### When NOT to Use
- Code implementation, tests, or debugging — use `sk-code`.
- Git worktree, branch, commit, PR, or release work — use `sk-git`.
- Spec-folder workflow / memory / save context — use `system-spec-kit`.
- A measured Style Reference (design tokens extracted from a live source) — use `sk-design-md-generator`.
- The `shared/` backbone is consumed by the packets, not invoked as a user workflow.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is **registry-driven at runtime and packet-authored at source** in two stages. Stage 1 (hub → mode): each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections that the hub reads without re-deriving mappings during a request. The advisor routes any documentation/authoring query to the single identity `sk-doc`; the hub then picks the packet. Stage 2 (mode → leaves): the root `ROUTER.md` maps the request's authoring intent to the exact packet-local leaf resources that mode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router never re-decides the mode.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-doc --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `sk-doc`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.

### Surface Router — per-intent leaf sets

Stage 2 of routing lives in `ROUTER.md` at the hub root, next to `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. It defines the per-intent leaf model (document quality, optimization, skill creation, parent-hub creation, agent creation, command creation, the paired agent-plus-command lane, flowcharts, the human-voice pass, playbooks, feature catalogs, READMEs, changelogs, benchmarks, diffs, packet goals, repo rules, and the explicit full-toolkit intent), the machine-readable `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block that the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse, and the how-to-read rules (dominant intent → one leaf set; near-tied intents → deduped union; no keyword match → hub UNKNOWN fallback, never a silent default). Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path is packet-qualified or an authored shared-alias disk path, and each converts to the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair at the one contract boundary.

`ROUTER.md` stays a separate document on purpose: the router-replay contract resolves the hub's mode from `hub-router.json` and reads the leaf sets from the surface document — the machine block must not move into `SKILL.md` (the replay would treat it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection) or into `hub-router.json` (schema handoff-ambiguity rule). The `shared/` backbone stays the universal sk-create-quality-control source; the surface router only selects leaves.

### The discriminator
- **`workflowMode`** — the public packet key (e.g. `sk-create-skill`, `sk-create-quality-control`). `sk-create-skill-parent` is a second mode over the same `sk-create-skill` packet.
- **`packetKind`** — `workflow` for every sk-doc packet (there is no surface axis; the sk-create-quality-control pipeline is universal doctrine in `shared/`, not orthogonal stack-evidence).
- **`backendKind`** — `template-scaffold` for the create-* generators, `sk-create-quality-control` for the sk-create-quality-control mode.

### Routing rule
```
SKILL_ROOT = path containing this SKILL.md
REGISTRY = SKILL_ROOT / "mode-registry.json"
HUB_ROUTER = SKILL_ROOT / "hub-router.json"

UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
    "Confirm whether this is sk-create-skill, sk-create-skill-parent, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command, sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark, sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter, sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, or sk-create-quality-control work",
    "Confirm the target document or component being authored, scaffolded, or reviewed",
    "Provide the available inputs: existing doc, source material, or scaffold parameters",
    "Confirm the validation expectations before completion (DQI/HVR scoring, validate.sh, or packet-specific checks)",
]

def _guard_in_skill(relative_path):
  resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
  resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
  if resolved.suffix.lower() not in {".md", ".json"}:
    raise ValueError("only skill-local markdown/json router resources are routable")
  return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()

def load_if_available(relative_path, seen):
  guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
  if guarded not in seen and (SKILL_ROOT / guarded).exists():
    load(guarded)
    seen.add(guarded)
    return True
  return False

seen = set()
if not REGISTRY.exists() or not HUB_ROUTER.exists():
  return defer("router metadata missing; inspect sk-doc/mode-registry.json and sk-doc/hub-router.json")

read mode-registry.json and hub-router.json
classify the request to one or more workflowMode values using hub-router.json
  (dominant authoring/quality intent; a command like /create:agent resolves directly)

if confidence is low, intent is contradictory, or routerPolicy.defaultMode is null and no mode wins:
  for resource in hub_router.routerPolicy.defaultResource:   # the ordered defer set, never hardcoded here
    load_if_available(resource, seen)
  return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK with disambiguation_checklist = UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST

for each resolved workflowMode:
  entry = the matching mode-registry.json modes[] item
  if entry is missing or entry.packetKind != "workflow":
    return defer("unknown sk-doc workflowMode; extend mode-registry.json and create a packet first")
  if not load_if_available(f"{entry.packet}/SKILL.md", seen):
    return defer("registered packet SKILL.md is missing; repair the packet before routing")

return single or orderedBundle according to hub-router.json routerPolicy.outcomes
```
`routerPolicy.defaultMode` is `null`: an unclear documentation intent asks for disambiguation rather than forcing a stale default. `hub-router.json` carries the router signals, vocabulary classes, default fallback resource, and bundle rules. Outcomes are `single`, `orderedBundle`, or `defer` — there is no `surfaceBundle` (no surface axis).

Per-packet behavior is **not flattened**: each packet keeps its own authoring contract, references, assets, scripts, and templates.

This hub does **not** use keyed resource discovery (`references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/`) at the hub root: there are no hub-root `references/` or `assets/` directories, and packet resources stay inside their owning packet or the shared backbone. If a future workflow needs keyed resource subdirectories, add that behavior inside the owning packet using guarded runtime discovery; do not hardcode resource inventories in this hub.

---

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

### Layout
```
sk-doc/
  SKILL.md               # this routing hub (no per-packet logic)
  ROUTER.md              # stage-two surface router (authoring intent -> leaf sets)
  mode-registry.json     # the fifteen-mode discriminator + advisorRouting (single source of truth)
  hub-router.json        # router signals + vocabulary classes
  description.json       # hub advisor descriptor
  graph-metadata.json    # the ONE advisor identity for the whole skill
  changelog/  manual-testing-playbook/  benchmark/  feature-catalog/
  sk-create-skill/  sk-create-readme/  sk-create-agent/  sk-create-command/
  sk-create-feature-catalog/  sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/
  sk-create-benchmark/  sk-create-changelog/  sk-create-diff/
  sk-create-repo-rule/  sk-create-frontmatter/  sk-create-goal/
  sk-create-with-human-voice/  sk-create-quality-control/    # nested workflow packets
  scripts/               # facade symlinks -> shared/ + owning packets (tool paths only)
  shared/                # sk-create-quality-control backbone: validators, global standards, shared assets
```

Each packet is self-contained (its own `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `changelog/`, and moved `references/`/`assets/`/`scripts/`) and carries **no** `graph-metadata.json`, so the advisor discovers exactly one `sk-doc` identity.

### Shared backbone
`shared/` holds the universal sk-create-quality-control pipeline consumed by every packet: generic validator scripts (`shared/scripts/`), cross-cutting standards and vocabulary (`shared/references/`), and shared templates (`shared/assets/`). The generic validator `shared/scripts/cite-drift-scan.mjs` counts and resolves the `<path>.<ext>:<line>` citations in every tracked skill doc and makes zero model calls by default, while `--jev` runs the backend and needs `--out <dir>` so every call is recorded; the Jev arm and the advisory live in the sibling `shared/scripts/classifier-cite-drift-scan.mjs`. `validate_document.py` runs the same check as a non-blocking advisory on the document it validates: it prints `cite-drift advisory:` lines only when a Jev credential is stored, never changes the exit code, and `JEV_FEATURE_CITE_DRIFT=0` (older name: `SKDOC_CITE_DRIFT_CHECK=0`) skips it. The `sk-doc/scripts/` root directory keeps facade symlinks pointing inward to `shared/` and the owning packets so tool paths resolve. There are no hub-root `assets/` or `references/` aggregation directories: consumers reference each packet's own `assets/`/`references/` or the `shared/` backbone directly.

---

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS
- **ALWAYS** resolve a packet through `mode-registry.json`; never hardcode a router mapping in the hub.
- **ALWAYS** keep authoring contracts in the packets; the hub stays routing-only.
- **ALWAYS** keep exactly one `graph-metadata.json` (this hub's) so the advisor sees one identity.
- **ALWAYS** keep the root `ROUTER.md` `RESOURCE_MAP` in sync with `leaf-manifest.json` and `leaf-aliases.json` — the leaf sets dual-read to canonical typed pairs at the one contract boundary.
- **ALWAYS** keep the sk-create-quality-control pipeline as one shared source under `shared/`, consumed by the packets.
- **ALWAYS** keep changelogs as real files at the hub and in each packet — never symlinked.

### ⛔ NEVER
- **NEVER** add a `graph-metadata.json` inside a packet or `shared/`.
- **NEVER** put per-packet authoring logic in the hub.
- **NEVER** add a surface axis or a `surfaceBundle` outcome — sk-doc is workflow-only.

### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
- A new documentation workflow is needed — extend `mode-registry.json` and open a packet; do not bolt logic onto the hub.
- A packet would become a near-empty shell (generic doctrine, no type-specific behavior) — fold it into `shared/` instead.

---

- Registry: `mode-registry.json` (fifteen modes across fourteen packets, `packetKind: workflow`).

<skill_content name="sk-doc">
# Skill: sk-doc

<!-- Keywords: sk-doc, documentation, markdown, authoring, parent-hub, mode-registry, hub-router, workflowmode, packetkind, sk-create-skill, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command, sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark, sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter, sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, sk-create-quality-control, human-voice-rules, hvr, shared-backbone, create-quality-control-pipeline -->

# Documentation Authoring Hub (sk-doc)

One advisor identity, fifteen workflow modes across fourteen packets, one shared sk-create-quality-control backbone. `sk-doc` is the parent hub for documentation and OpenCode-component authoring. It holds NO per-packet logic: it routes by `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json`, and each packet keeps its own contract in its nested folder. The cross-cutting sk-create-quality-control pipeline (validators, global standards, frontmatter/llms/template assets) lives once in `shared/` and is consumed by every packet.

**Version authority.** This file's `version` frontmatter is the hub's release version and matches the newest entry under `changelog/`; `description.json`, `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` carry the same value, so every hub-root JSON routing file states the same release; `ROUTER.md` keeps its own document version.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

Use this skill for documentation and OpenCode-component authoring, and for document-quality work. The hub classifies the request, resolves a `workflowMode`, and loads the matching nested packet.

| Mode | Use it for | Packet | Command |
|------|------------|--------|---------|
| **sk-create-skill** | Scaffold an OpenCode skill (and, via `sk-create-skill-parent`, a parent hub with nested mode packets) | `sk-create-skill/` | `/create:skill`, `/create:skill-parent` |
| **sk-create-readme** | Author a folder README, general or code-folder | `sk-create-readme/` | `/create:readme` |
| **sk-create-agent** | Scaffold an OpenCode agent (permission/authority frontmatter) | `sk-create-agent/` | `/create:agent` |
| **sk-create-command** | Scaffold an OpenCode slash command (argument-hint + allowed-tools + router/presentation split) | `sk-create-command/` | `/create:command` |
| **sk-create-feature-catalog** | Author a feature-catalog inventory package | `sk-create-feature-catalog/` | `/create:feature-catalog` |
| **sk-create-manual-testing-playbook** | Author a manual-testing-playbook package | `sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/` | `/create:manual-testing-playbook` |
| **sk-create-benchmark** | Author MCP-promotion and behavior packages or inputs | `sk-create-benchmark/` | `/create:benchmark` |
| **sk-create-changelog** | Author a global or packet-local changelog entry (version bump + topology-aware placement) | `sk-create-changelog/` | `/create:changelog` |
| **sk-create-diff** | Produce a local, Git-free before/after review of an edited document (text/Markdown/HTML/DOCX/text-PDF) as a self-contained HTML report | `sk-create-diff/` | `/create:diff` |
| **sk-create-repo-rule** | Create, revise or retire a repo-local rule under `repo-rules/` and wire it into `REPO RULES.md` (four decision tests refuse most requests) | `sk-create-repo-rule/` | `/create:repo-rule` |
| **sk-create-with-human-voice** | Apply the Human Voice Rules to prose, or score prose against them, with a scope gate and a re-scan | `sk-create-with-human-voice/` | `/create:with-human-voice` |
| **sk-create-frontmatter** | Own the YAML frontmatter contract: per-class field rules, the description budget, and the 4-part `version` derivation | `sk-create-frontmatter/` | — (routes via aliases) |
| **sk-create-goal** | Author or revise a packet `goal.md`: the durable directive, three to seven self-contained completion criteria, and the phase-parent binding table (session-goal setting stays with the goal hooks) | `sk-create-goal/` | `/create:goal` |
| **sk-create-quality-control** | Validate / score / optimize an EXISTING document (extract → DQI → HVR → validate) | `sk-create-quality-control/` | (routes via aliases) |

### When NOT to Use
- Code implementation, tests, or debugging — use `sk-code`.
- Git worktree, branch, commit, PR, or release work — use `sk-git`.
- Spec-folder workflow / memory / save context — use `system-spec-kit`.
- A measured Style Reference (design tokens extracted from a live source) — use `sk-design-md-generator`.
- The `shared/` backbone is consumed by the packets, not invoked as a user workflow.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

Routing is **registry-driven at runtime and packet-authored at source** in two stages. Stage 1 (hub → mode): each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections that the hub reads without re-deriving mappings during a request. The advisor routes any documentation/authoring query to the single identity `sk-doc`; the hub then picks the packet. Stage 2 (mode → leaves): the root `ROUTER.md` maps the request's authoring intent to the exact packet-local leaf resources that mode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router never re-decides the mode.

> **Compiled routing (default-on, flag-gated, additive).** Resolve the mode via the compiled router contract first:
> ```bash
> node .skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-doc --prompt "<task>"
> ```
> Follow the returned decision — `route` (use its `targets`), `clarify`/`defer` (disambiguate), `reject` (refuse). On a `{"servingAuthority":"legacy"}` sentinel or any error, use the routing below. The front door self-gates on serving-authority. Compiled routing is now the default for `sk-doc`; set `SPECKIT_COMPILED_ROUTING=0` to force legacy routing fleet-wide — the explicit kill-switch.

### Surface Router — per-intent leaf sets

Stage 2 of routing lives in `ROUTER.md` at the hub root, next to `SKILL.md` and `README.md`. It defines the per-intent leaf model (document quality, optimization, skill creation, parent-hub creation, agent creation, command creation, the paired agent-plus-command lane, flowcharts, the human-voice pass, playbooks, feature catalogs, READMEs, changelogs, benchmarks, diffs, packet goals, repo rules, and the explicit full-toolkit intent), the machine-readable `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block that the deterministic router-replay and benchmarks parse, and the how-to-read rules (dominant intent → one leaf set; near-tied intents → deduped union; no keyword match → hub UNKNOWN fallback, never a silent default). Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path is packet-qualified or an authored shared-alias disk path, and each converts to the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair at the one contract boundary.

`ROUTER.md` stays a separate document on purpose: the router-replay contract resolves the hub's mode from `hub-router.json` and reads the leaf sets from the surface document — the machine block must not move into `SKILL.md` (the replay would treat it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection) or into `hub-router.json` (schema handoff-ambiguity rule). The `shared/` backbone stays the universal sk-create-quality-control source; the surface router only selects leaves.

### The discriminator
- **`workflowMode`** — the public packet key (e.g. `sk-create-skill`, `sk-create-quality-control`). `sk-create-skill-parent` is a second mode over the same `sk-create-skill` packet.
- **`packetKind`** — `workflow` for every sk-doc packet (there is no surface axis; the sk-create-quality-control pipeline is universal doctrine in `shared/`, not orthogonal stack-evidence).
- **`backendKind`** — `template-scaffold` for the create-* generators, `sk-create-quality-control` for the sk-create-quality-control mode.

### Routing rule
```
SKILL_ROOT = path containing this SKILL.md
REGISTRY = SKILL_ROOT / "mode-registry.json"
HUB_ROUTER = SKILL_ROOT / "hub-router.json"

UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [
    "Confirm whether this is sk-create-skill, sk-create-skill-parent, sk-create-readme, sk-create-agent, sk-create-command, sk-create-feature-catalog, sk-create-manual-testing-playbook, sk-create-benchmark, sk-create-changelog, sk-create-diff, sk-create-repo-rule, sk-create-frontmatter, sk-create-goal, sk-create-with-human-voice, or sk-create-quality-control work",
    "Confirm the target document or component being authored, scaffolded, or reviewed",
    "Provide the available inputs: existing doc, source material, or scaffold parameters",
    "Confirm the validation expectations before completion (DQI/HVR scoring, validate.sh, or packet-specific checks)",
]

def _guard_in_skill(relative_path):
  resolved = (SKILL_ROOT / relative_path).resolve()
  resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT)
  if resolved.suffix.lower() not in {".md", ".json"}:
    raise ValueError("only skill-local markdown/json router resources are routable")
  return resolved.relative_to(SKILL_ROOT).as_posix()

def load_if_available(relative_path, seen):
  guarded = _guard_in_skill(relative_path)
  if guarded not in seen and (SKILL_ROOT / guarded).exists():
    load(guarded)
    seen.add(guarded)
    return True
  return False

seen = set()
if not REGISTRY.exists() or not HUB_ROUTER.exists():
  return defer("router metadata missing; inspect sk-doc/mode-registry.json and sk-doc/hub-router.json")

read mode-registry.json and hub-router.json
classify the request to one or more workflowMode values using hub-router.json
  (dominant authoring/quality intent; a command like /create:agent resolves directly)

if confidence is low, intent is contradictory, or routerPolicy.defaultMode is null and no mode wins:
  for resource in hub_router.routerPolicy.defaultResource:   # the ordered defer set, never hardcoded here
    load_if_available(resource, seen)
  return UNKNOWN_FALLBACK with disambiguation_checklist = UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST

for each resolved workflowMode:
  entry = the matching mode-registry.json modes[] item
  if entry is missing or entry.packetKind != "workflow":
    return defer("unknown sk-doc workflowMode; extend mode-registry.json and create a packet first")
  if not load_if_available(f"{entry.packet}/SKILL.md", seen):
    return defer("registered packet SKILL.md is missing; repair the packet before routing")

return single or orderedBundle according to hub-router.json routerPolicy.outcomes
```
`routerPolicy.defaultMode` is `null`: an unclear documentation intent asks for disambiguation rather than forcing a stale default. `hub-router.json` carries the router signals, vocabulary classes, default fallback resource, and bundle rules. Outcomes are `single`, `orderedBundle`, or `defer` — there is no `surfaceBundle` (no surface axis).

Per-packet behavior is **not flattened**: each packet keeps its own authoring contract, references, assets, scripts, and templates.

This hub does **not** use keyed resource discovery (`references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/`) at the hub root: there are no hub-root `references/` or `assets/` directories, and packet resources stay inside their owning packet or the shared backbone. If a future workflow needs keyed resource subdirectories, add that behavior inside the owning packet using guarded runtime discovery; do not hardcode resource inventories in this hub.

---

## 3. HOW IT WORKS

### Layout
```
sk-doc/
  SKILL.md               # this routing hub (no per-packet logic)
  ROUTER.md              # stage-two surface router (authoring intent -> leaf sets)
  mode-registry.json     # the fifteen-mode discriminator + advisorRouting (single source of truth)
  hub-router.json        # router signals + vocabulary classes
  description.json       # hub advisor descriptor
  graph-metadata.json    # the ONE advisor identity for the whole skill
  changelog/  manual-testing-playbook/  benchmark/  feature-catalog/
  sk-create-skill/  sk-create-readme/  sk-create-agent/  sk-create-command/
  sk-create-feature-catalog/  sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/
  sk-create-benchmark/  sk-create-changelog/  sk-create-diff/
  sk-create-repo-rule/  sk-create-frontmatter/  sk-create-goal/
  sk-create-with-human-voice/  sk-create-quality-control/    # nested workflow packets
  scripts/               # facade symlinks -> shared/ + owning packets (tool paths only)
  shared/                # sk-create-quality-control backbone: validators, global standards, shared assets
```

Each packet is self-contained (its own `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `changelog/`, and moved `references/`/`assets/`/`scripts/`) and carries **no** `graph-metadata.json`, so the advisor discovers exactly one `sk-doc` identity.

### Shared backbone
`shared/` holds the universal sk-create-quality-control pipeline consumed by every packet: generic validator scripts (`shared/scripts/`), cross-cutting standards and vocabulary (`shared/references/`), and shared templates (`shared/assets/`). The generic validator `shared/scripts/cite-drift-scan.mjs` counts and resolves the `<path>.<ext>:<line>` citations in every tracked skill doc and makes zero model calls by default, while `--jev` runs the backend and needs `--out <dir>` so every call is recorded; the Jev arm and the advisory live in the sibling `shared/scripts/classifier-cite-drift-scan.mjs`. `validate_document.py` runs the same check as a non-blocking advisory on the document it validates: it prints `cite-drift advisory:` lines only when a Jev credential is stored, never changes the exit code, and `JEV_FEATURE_CITE_DRIFT=0` (older name: `SKDOC_CITE_DRIFT_CHECK=0`) skips it. The `sk-doc/scripts/` root directory keeps facade symlinks pointing inward to `shared/` and the owning packets so tool paths resolve. There are no hub-root `assets/` or `references/` aggregation directories: consumers reference each packet's own `assets/`/`references/` or the `shared/` backbone directly.

---

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS
- **ALWAYS** resolve a packet through `mode-registry.json`; never hardcode a router mapping in the hub.
- **ALWAYS** keep authoring contracts in the packets; the hub stays routing-only.
- **ALWAYS** keep exactly one `graph-metadata.json` (this hub's) so the advisor sees one identity.
- **ALWAYS** keep the root `ROUTER.md` `RESOURCE_MAP` in sync with `leaf-manifest.json` and `leaf-aliases.json` — the leaf sets dual-read to canonical typed pairs at the one contract boundary.
- **ALWAYS** keep the sk-create-quality-control pipeline as one shared source under `shared/`, consumed by the packets.
- **ALWAYS** keep changelogs as real files at the hub and in each packet — never symlinked.

### ⛔ NEVER
- **NEVER** add a `graph-metadata.json` inside a packet or `shared/`.
- **NEVER** put per-packet authoring logic in the hub.
- **NEVER** add a surface axis or a `surfaceBundle` outcome — sk-doc is workflow-only.

### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
- A new documentation workflow is needed — extend `mode-registry.json` and open a packet; do not bolt logic onto the hub.
- A packet would become a near-empty shell (generic doctrine, no type-specific behavior) — fold it into `shared/` instead.

---

## 5. REFERENCES

- Registry: `mode-registry.json` (fifteen modes across fourteen packets, `packetKind: workflow`).
- Hub router: `hub-router.json` (signals + vocabulary classes).
- Surface router: `ROUTER.md` (authoring intent to packet-local leaf sets).
- Advisor descriptor: `description.json`; skill-graph identity: `graph-metadata.json`.
- Packets: `sk-create-skill/`, `sk-create-readme/`, `sk-create-agent/`, `sk-create-command/`, `sk-create-feature-catalog/`, `sk-create-manual-testing-playbook/`, `sk-create-benchmark/`, `sk-create-changelog/`, `sk-create-diff/`, `sk-create-repo-rule/`, `sk-create-frontmatter/`, `sk-create-goal/`, `sk-create-with-human-voice/`, `sk-create-quality-control/`.
- Shared backbone: `shared/scripts/`, `shared/references/`, `shared/assets/`.
- Parent-skill pattern: `sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md`.

26: # Rule: Communication prose
27: 
28: > Routed from [`REPO RULES.md`](../../REPO%20RULES.md). Load before writing any substantive reply.
29: > Expands `AGENTS.md`, never overrides it. Where they appear to disagree, `AGENTS.md` wins and this file is wrong. Say so.
30: 
31: ## Fires when
32: 
33: - Drafting or editing a sentence a reader will read.
34: - Choosing between a plain and an exact word.
35: - Placing a dash, colon or semicolon.
36: - Splitting or joining sentences.
37: - Writing a paragraph.
38: 
39: ## The rule
40: 
41: **A sentence carries one idea, a paragraph stands alone, the words are plain and the
42: punctuation never trips the reader.**
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 1. SENTENCES AND PARAGRAPHS
47: 
48: **One idea per sentence.** Short, declarative, subject-verb-object where that reads
49: naturally. When a sentence stacks clauses, split it.
50: 
51: **Atomic paragraphs.** Each chunk stands alone. A reader who lands mid-reply should be
52: able to act on the paragraph in front of them without reconstructing the four above it.
53: 
54: **Vary the rhythm** of sentence length and structure. Prefer prose when a list would
55: fragment a single argument.
56: 
57: The failure this prevents: a technically correct reply the reader has to parse twice.
58: 
59: **State the relation between sentences.** Each sentence opens by saying how it attaches
60: to the one before: because, but, therefore, for example.
61: 
62: The failure this prevents: juxtaposition fakes a logical link the writer never stated,
63: and the reader supplies their own, and supplies a different one.
64: 
65: **Name the mechanism.** When a sentence explains how something works, it names the
66: moving parts: what acts, what it acts on, what changes.
67: 
68: The failure this prevents: a model whose moving parts are never named, so the reader
69: can remember it and cannot check it.
70: 
71: ---
72: 
73: ## 2. WORDS
74: 
75: Plain words by default. Reserve exact names for the things that have them, languages,
76: frameworks, APIs, dependencies, commands.
77: 
78: Introduce unavoidable jargon one term at a time, in a sentence that defines it by use.
79: 
80: The failure this prevents: the reader stops reading and starts decoding, and stops
81: noticing whether they agree.
82: 
83: Do not ship replies in terse machine register. Replace arrows or symbols standing in for
84: verbs with action words. For stacked noun phrases, say who does what, using the
85: [HVR nominalization guidance](../skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md#nominalization-and-stacked-compression).
86: Explain each ID, abbreviation or status code in plain words. Say what each bare count
87: or label measures and what it means. Turn sentence fragments into complete sentences
88: with a subject and verb, and join two of them with a full stop or a conjunction, never a
89: semicolon. The failure this prevents: readers have to guess at the action,
90: referent or result.
91: 
92: **Name an identifier only where the reader acts on it.** A path, hash, flag or ID earns its
93: place when the reader will run, open or check it. Elsewhere, say what the thing is in plain
94: words.
95: 
96: **One or two numbers to a sentence.** When the numbers are the point, give each its own
97: sentence or bullet.
98: 
99: The failure this prevents: a reply dense with names and figures the reader cannot use,
100: which buries the few they need.
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 3. PUNCTUATION THE READER TRIPS ON
105: 
106: **Never use an em dash.** Replace it with a comma, a full stop or a colon, whichever the
107: sentence actually wanted.
108: 
109: - **No semicolon.** Two sentences, or a conjunction.
110: - **No serial comma.** Drop it before the `and` or `or` that closes a list.
111: 
112: **The failure this prevents:** dashes read as authored voice to a human and as a tell to a
113: reader who has seen a lot of generated text.
114: 
115: The full standard is the Human Voice Rules, which `sk-doc` routes to. Load all of it when writing a document.
116: 
117: **In a reply, take its voice half and leave its document half.** The voice directives, the
118: vocabulary lists and the tell lists apply to anything a reader reads. The document-structure
119: sections do not. A message that presents the result of a long run is a reply by delivery and
120: a document by content, and it takes the voice half like any other reply.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 4. CONCISE IS NOT COMPRESSED
125: 
126: Concise cuts what the reader does not need and stops.
127: Compressed cuts further and takes the connective tissue with it: the because, the second
128: half of a contrast, the noun that a later "this" points back to. After a cut, check the
129: joints. If a sentence now opens on a "this" that the previous sentence no longer feeds,
130: the connection was the thing that got cut.
131: 
132: The failure this prevents: brevity that deletes the connective tissue and turns the
133: reply telegraphic, the reader rebuilds the argument the reply no longer states.
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 5. WHAT THIS RULE IS NOT
138: 
139: - **Not a whole-reply rule.** Length, filler, tables and recovery live in
140:   [`communication.md`](communication.md), this rule stops where the reply as a whole begins.
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: ## 6. SELF-CHECK
145: 
146: - [ ] Every sentence carries one idea, and no sentence stacks clauses a reader has to unpick.
147: - [ ] Every paragraph stands on its own, and the rhythm varies rather than marching.
148: - [ ] Replies use action words for arrows and symbols, say who does what, explain IDs,
149:   abbreviations and status codes, state what bare counts and labels mean, and turn
150:   fragments into full sentences.
151: - [ ] Each sentence says how it attaches to the one before, rather than sitting beside it.
152: - [ ] Where a sentence explains how something works, it names the moving part.
153: - [ ] Plain words, with exact names kept only for the things that have them.
154: - [ ] No em dash, no semicolon, no serial comma.
155: - [ ] Every path, hash, flag or ID in the reply is one the reader will act on, and no sentence carries more than two numbers.
156: - [ ] Nothing was compressed past the point where the reader has to re-expand it.

83: Do not ship replies in terse machine register. Replace arrows or symbols standing in for
84: verbs with action words. For stacked noun phrases, say who does what, using the
85: [HVR nominalization guidance](../skills/sk-doc/sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md#nominalization-and-stacked-compression).
86: Explain each ID, abbreviation or status code in plain words. Say what each bare count
87: or label measures and what it means. Turn sentence fragments into complete sentences
88: with a subject and verb, and join two of them with a full stop or a conjunction, never a
89: semicolon. The failure this prevents: readers have to guess at the action,
90: referent or result.
91: 
92: **Name an identifier only where the reader acts on it.** A path, hash, flag or ID earns its
93: place when the reader will run, open or check it. Elsewhere, say what the thing is in plain
94: words.
95: 
96: **One or two numbers to a sentence.** When the numbers are the point, give each its own
97: sentence or bullet.
98: 
99: The failure this prevents: a reply dense with names and figures the reader cannot use,
100: which buries the few they need.
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 3. PUNCTUATION THE READER TRIPS ON
105: 
106: **Never use an em dash.** Replace it with a comma, a full stop or a colon, whichever the
107: sentence actually wanted.
108: 
109: - **No semicolon.** Two sentences, or a conjunction.
110: - **No serial comma.** Drop it before the `and` or `or` that closes a list.
111: 
112: **The failure this prevents:** dashes read as authored voice to a human and as a tell to a
113: reader who has seen a lot of generated text.
114: 
115: The full standard is the Human Voice Rules, which `sk-doc` routes to. Load all of it when writing a document.
116: 
117: **In a reply, take its voice half and leave its document half.** The voice directives, the
118: vocabulary lists and the tell lists apply to anything a reader reads. The document-structure
119: sections do not. A message that presents the result of a long run is a reply by delivery and
120: a document by content, and it takes the voice half like any other reply.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ## 4. CONCISE IS NOT COMPRESSED
125: 
126: Concise cuts what the reader does not need and stops.
127: Compressed cuts further and takes the connective tissue with it: the because, the second
128: half of a contrast, the noun that a later "this" points back to. After a cut, check the
129: joints. If a sentence now opens on a "this" that the previous sentence no longer feeds,
130: the connection was the thing that got cut.
131: 
132: The failure this prevents: brevity that deletes the connective tissue and turns the
133: reply telegraphic, the reader rebuilds the argument the reply no longer states.
134: 
135: ---
136: 
137: ## 5. WHAT THIS RULE IS NOT
138: 
139: - **Not a whole-reply rule.** Length, filler, tables and recovery live in
140:   [`communication.md`](communication.md), this rule stops where the reply as a whole begins.
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: ## 6. SELF-CHECK
145: 
146: - [ ] Every sentence carries one idea, and no sentence stacks clauses a reader has to unpick.
147: - [ ] Every paragraph stands on its own, and the rhythm varies rather than marching.
148: - [ ] Replies use action words for arrows and symbols, say who does what, explain IDs,
149:   abbreviations and status codes, state what bare counts and labels mean, and turn
150:   fragments into full sentences.
151: - [ ] Each sentence says how it attaches to the one before, rather than sitting beside it.
152: - [ ] Where a sentence explains how something works, it names the moving part.
153: - [ ] Plain words, with exact names kept only for the things that have them.
154: - [ ] No em dash, no semicolon, no serial comma.
155: - [ ] Every path, hash, flag or ID in the reply is one the reader will act on, and no sentence carries more than two numbers.
156: - [ ] Nothing was compressed past the point where the reader has to re-expand it.

It prints `OWNER006=LEDGER_MISSING` when the ledger is absent. Otherwise it prints `OWNER006_TOTAL=<n>`, `OWNER006_OPEN=<m>` and one `COVERED` or `OPEN` line per owner `006` row. Verify: `grep -cE '^(COVERED|OPEN) ' "$A/owner-006-status.txt"` prints `n` and `grep -c '^OPEN ' "$A/owner-006-status.txt"` prints `m`, so the status file matches both summary numbers.   cd "$WORKTREE"
